title: Patidar's 135 Off 48 and Suryakumar's 82 Off 29 Light Up SMAT
excerpt: Madhya Pradesh posted a tournament-record 250 for 6 to rout Assam, while Mumbai chased 198 in 15.4 overs against Gujarat in Monday's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy action.
body:
• Rajat Patidar struck an unbeaten 135 off 48 balls, with eight fours and 13 sixes, as Madhya Pradesh posted 250 for 6 and beat Assam by 131 runs in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy in New Chandigarh.
  • Patidar is the first Madhya Pradesh batter to score a century in the tournament. His hundred came off 41 balls, and he shared a 153-run fourth-wicket stand with Shivang Kumar, who made 61 off 38.
  • Suryakumar Yadav hit 82 off 29 balls, with nine fours and seven sixes, as Mumbai chased 198 in 15.4 overs to beat Gujarat by five wickets in Kolkata.
  • It was Suryakumar's second explosive innings in two matches, after an unbeaten 60 off 21 against Hyderabad, and it keeps the selection debate around both batters live.

Two chases and one rout defined Monday's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy action. In New Chandigarh, Rajat Patidar's unbeaten 135 off 48 balls powered Madhya Pradesh to 250 for 6, their highest total in the tournament, and a 131-run win over Assam. In Kolkata, Suryakumar Yadav's 82 off 29 balls made a target of 198 look small, as Mumbai beat Gujarat by five wickets with 26 balls to spare, according to reports from RevSportz, Wisden and CricTracker.

Patidar turns 57 for 3 into 250

Patidar walked in at No. 5 with Madhya Pradesh on 57 for 3 in 7.4 overs. By the end of the 15th over he was 48 off 24 balls. He then scored 87 off his last 24, reaching his century on the second ball of the 19th over, his 41st delivery, and finishing unbeaten on 135 off 48 with eight fours and 13 sixes, a strike rate of 281.25. Shivang Kumar held the other end with 61 off 38, and together they added 153 runs off 62 balls for the fourth wicket.

The innings set two state marks. Patidar is the first Madhya Pradesh batter to score a century in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, and his 13 sixes are the most by a Madhya Pradesh batter in a single innings in the tournament. The team's 250 for 6 beat their previous highest T20 total of 244 for 4 against Meghalaya in 2019. Assam were bowled out for 119 in 17.4 overs, with Kumar Kartikeya taking 3 for 17 in his four overs and Avesh Khan two for 20 in three. It was Patidar's second hundred in T20 cricket.

Suryakumar makes 198 look short

Gujarat posted 197 all out in 19.2 overs at the Jadavpur University Second Campus Ground in Kolkata, a total built the hard way after Shardul Thakur and Atharva Ankolekar took three wickets each. A lower-order counterattack, led by Ashutosh Sharma's 42 off 22 balls and Vishal Jayswal's 38 off 21, dragged Gujarat to a competitive score.

Mumbai's reply removed the contest early. Suryakumar brought up his half-century off 18 balls and was out in the 11th over, bowled by Ravi Bishnoi, for 82 off 29 balls, with nine fours and seven sixes at a strike rate of 282.76. Sarfaraz Khan finished the chase with an unbeaten 40 off 17 balls, and Mumbai reached 201 for 5 in 15.4 overs. Across his first two matches of the tournament, Suryakumar has scored 142 runs off 50 balls, following his unbeaten 60 off 21 against Hyderabad in Mumbai's opener.

What it means

Both innings land in the middle of a selection argument. Patidar, who captains Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the IPL, has played Tests and an ODI for India but is yet to debut in T20 internationals, and Wisden notes that even a 501-run IPL 2026 campaign was not enough to win him a T20I place. Suryakumar's case runs the other way: CricTracker reports he was stripped of the T20I captaincy and dropped after a prolonged slump, following his final international outing on March 8, 2026, when he led India to victory in the T20 World Cup final. Two innings at a strike rate above 280 will, as CricTracker puts it, give the selectors considerable material to assess. The Elite group stage continues this week, and both batters have made sure their next innings will be watched as auditions.
